expectedOutcome: After completing the plan, learners can choose a two-pointer, search, tree/graph, or dynamic-programming framework from a problem's characteristics and explain its state, invariants, and critical boundaries.
goal: Build a stable process for recognizing problem structures, applying algorithm frameworks, and checking boundary conditions.
notRecommendedFor: There is no data structure at all.

phases.focus: Start with arrays and linked lists, practicing fast/slow pointers, left/right pointers, and in-place modification.
phases.title: Linear Structures and Two-Pointer Frameworks

phases.focus: Practice reusable frameworks for sliding windows, binary-search boundaries, prefix sums, and difference arrays.
phases.title: Sliding Windows, Binary Search, and Preprocessing

phases.focus: Understand recursive and backtracking search through decision trees, state restoration, and shortest-step models.
phases.title: Recursion, Backtracking, and BFS

phases.focus: Build a tree-problem framework around traversal positions, subtree return values, and binary search tree properties.
phases.title: Binary-Tree Recursive Thinking

phases.focus: Progress from graph construction to topological sorting, connectivity, shortest paths, and minimum spanning trees.
phases.title: Graphs and Connectivity

phases.focus: Practice defining states, choices, transitions, and base cases across sequence and state-machine problems.
phases.title: Dynamic Programming State Design

phases.focus: Practice maintaining state with monotonic stacks, monotonic queues, priority queues, and cache structures.
phases.title: Monotonic Structures, Heaps, and Design

phases.focus: Use classic composite frameworks to test transfer, boundary control, and data-structure composition skills.
phases.title: High-Frequency Integrated Applications

prerequisites: Could do some Easy and Medium questions independently
recommendedFor: Wishing to create a cross-cutting solution framework
There's a lot of brushes, but there's not enough migration.
summary: Use eight weeks of focused practice to master core problem-solving frameworks for two pointers, search, trees and graphs, dynamic programming, and monotonic structures.
targetAudience: Learners who have practiced basic topics but have fragmented knowledge and want to connect problem types through reusable frameworks.
